question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Looking or sounding foreign, bizarre, strange, unfamiliar
solution:
The correct answer is "Outlandish". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given group of words needs a one-word substitute.
 
• The word "**outlandish**" means very **strange** or unusual; straying from the usual, customary, or anticipated.
 
• It also signifies **weird**, **uncommon**, peculiar, eccentric, erratic, odd, and challenging to comprehend or accept.
 
 
• Example: *Her opinions on how to raise children are somewhat outlandish.*
 
• *The show became increasingly outlandish as it went on.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the word "**outlandish**" is the **best** one-word substitute** for **the group of words "**looking or sounding foreign, bizarre, strange, unfamiliar**".
 
• The one-word substitute is: *Outlandish​*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Lets understand the meaning of the remaining words:

 
• **Outlaw**: (used in past times) a person who has done something **illegal** and is **hiding** to avoid being caught.

 
 
• Example: *Outlaw Robin Hood dwelt in the woods and robbed the wealthy to distribute to the needy.*
 
 
 
• **Outlay**: **money** that is spent, especially in order to start a **business** or project.
 
 
• Example: *The program will require a 3.6 million dollar upfront outlay.*
 
 
 
• **Outlast**: to **continue to exist **or to do something for a longer time than somebody/something.
 
 
• Example: *He won one of the best tennis matches ever, outlasting his opponent.*
